title: Headcount alignment for on-demand bursting and price-floor analysis
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet ties a small set of headcount hiring levers to on-demand/burst capacity policies and model pricing floors. Goal: give product and sales a quick sensitivity surface — if we hold price floors, how much HC flex (contractors vs perm) do we need to meet 95th-percentile bursts while preserving runway and margin targets.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline (current ops): 140 FTEs supporting inference infra + product; committed Dedicated capacity covers steady-state throughput.
- Stress case: 3x token surge over 12 weeks (marketing campaign + new partner). To avoid SLA violations we can: 1) deploy extra spot GPUs (costly short-term), 2) increase routing to higher-price dedicated pools, or 3) add contractor SRE/ops to scale orchestration / capacity provisioning.
- Our analysis shows a modest price-floor increase of 7–10% reduces required contractor headcount by ~40% in the surge window and keeps gross margin within target.

Assumptions and knobs (simple, editable):
- Token surge scenarios: +50%, +100%, +200%, +300% sustained for 4/8/12 weeks.
- Price-floor = minimum per-token price charged on hosted API for a given model family.
- Contractor cost (SRE/infra ops): $9k/week per contractor (including agency fees) for overtime/shift coverage; perm ramp cost = $18k/month fully loaded for onboarding + sustained salary.
- Spot GPU cost multiplier during surge: x1.6 baseline per-token infra cost.
- Dedicated surge routing: increases revenue per-token by price-floor uplift but reduces latency cost to customers (we assume 30% lower error rate).

Key tables (flattened spreadsheet view):

1) Headcount plan by scenario (rows show role groups; numbers = FTE-equivalents needed in surge window)

role,baseline_fte,need_+100pct,need_+200pct,need_+300pct,preferred_action
SRE/Infra,40,54,68,82,add-contractors+defer-perm
Runtime-Engineering,22,26,32,38,can-redirect-from-dedicated-roadmap
Platform-Eng,18,22,26,30,short-term-contracts
Customer-Success,10,14,18,22,temporary-cs-contracts
Billing/Finance,5,6,7,8,manual-billing-cover
Observability/Oncall,7,10,14,18,add-contractors
TOTAL,102,132,165,198,see-actions

Notes: "preferred_action" prioritizes speed-to-hire and reversible cost.

2) Pricing sensitivity surface (rows = price-floor uplift scenarios; columns = demand uplift; cells = net contribution margin delta vs baseline)

price_floor_uplift_pct,demand_uplift_+100pct,demand_uplift_+200pct,demand_uplift_+300pct
0%, -7.8%, -19.4%, -31.2%
+5%, -2.1%, -10.5%, -19.9%
+7.5%, +0.9%, -4.2%, -11.8%
+10%, +3.6%, +1.1%, -2.4%
+15%, +8.9%, +9.5%, +4.7%

Interpretation: small increases (7–10%) of price floor substantially reduce margin drag under large surges. +15% likely reduces churn but risks adoption friction; need A/B on a small customer cohort.

3) Cost tradeoff table (one-shot costs during a 12-week 3x surge)

action,est_infra_cost_delta,est_hc_cost_delta,est_revenue_delta,net_impact_on_margin
spin-up-spot-gpus,+$1.2M,+$0,+$0.0M,-$1.2M
hire-contractors(10 FTE-eq),+$0.3M,+$1.1M,+$0.6M,-$0.8M
raise-price-floor +7.5%,+$0.0M,+$0.0M,+$1.7M,+$1.7M
combo(raise 7.5% + 5 contractors),+$0.2M,+$0.55M,+$1.9M,+$1.15M

Interpretation: raising price-floor plus small HC flex provides best net margin in this simulated surge.

4) Runway and hiring policy impact (12-week window)
- Runway impact if we choose contractors instead of perm hires for surge: preserves 8–10 weeks of operating runway vs baseline (depends on booking).
- Perm hires: long-term capacity improves reliability but increases fixed burn; avoid for short-lived surges.

Sensitivity notes / behavioral risks:
- Demand elasticity unknown at higher price floors; recommend gated rollout to 10 largest enterprise customers to measure churn impact (pilot for 6 weeks).
- Competitors may hold price; raising floors can push certain price-sensitive SMB segments to alternatives. Recommend token-tiered floor (enterprise vs SMB).

Open calculations (editable cells in sheet):
- Baseline per-token infra cost: $0.00043 (current average across model families)
- Baseline revenue per-token: $0.0009 (average blended MSP mix)
- Conversion rates (if price-floor increased): assumed -3% elasticity per +5% price at SMB tier; enterprise elasticity -0.5% per +5% price.

Action items and recommended next steps (short list):
- Finance: produce gated cohort A/B plan for price-floor +7.5% (JIRA-FIN-3821) — owner: Priya (due 2026-03-12).
- Sales: identify 10 enterprise customers for pilot (owner: Liam) — due 2026-03-08.
- Eng/Product: prototype routing policy to prefer dedicated pool for customers in pilot and instrument latency/error metrics (owner: Jonah) — due 2026-03-19.
- People Ops: pre-approve contractor conversion pipeline and agency terms (owner: Sofia) — due 2026-03-10.

Questions for discussion at finance sync (2026-03-07):
1) Should we limit price-floor rollouts by region or SKU? EMEA price sensitivity historically ~10% lower ARPU.
2) If we choose contractors, what is the expected conversion rate to perm and cost of conversion? (assume 20–30% convert)
3) Do we want a separate SLA/discount schedule for customers impacted by routing to spot/backup models?

Appendix A: quick Monte Carlo notes (not baked into table)
- Ran 1k sims varying elasticity +/-50%, token-surge duration +/-25%, contractor fill time uniform(1..3 weeks).
- Median result: price-floor +7.5% + 5 contractors yields +3.2% incremental gross margin in the 12-week surge; 90% CI [-4.8%, +10.6%].

Appendix B: references and previous experiments
- price-floor-experiment-q4-2025 (pilot): small +5% floor on a subset of SKU led to -1.2% net churn on SMB after 4 weeks.
- dedicated-routing-latency-report-nov2025

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc — numbers are intentionally coarse. The sheet version contains live formulas and scenario toggles. Please comment inline or add rows with alternate assumptions.
